summary: Every surviving target and scenario string in verification-evidence.json is now substantively true against what its lane actually executes: all 26 kept claims, both narrowed claims and both withdrawals were re-verified from the source files, and both head-binding claims verify TRUE at the command level. The remaining problem is the audit trail, not the evidence content. The round-3 sweep (2 withdrawals + 2 narrowings) has no decision record anywhere in the repo, and verification-evidence.json's updated_at still reads 2026-07-31T11:07:47.702Z while its mtime is 2026-08-01T08:47:22Z, so the second edit round is invisible to any consumer. Separately the previously disclosed stale surface_hash condition is MISDESCRIBED: surface_hash covers source files, and all 8 were recomputed and every one MATCHES; observation prose was never hash-covered at all. Fix is cheap and non-destructive; regeneration by a real run is NOT required and would be worse.

findings.detail: The only retraction record is decision-1785540907191-6cebd89b whose reason enumerates exactly the round-2 items (the integration VET-S-6 scenario and the unit target test/managed-worktree-gate.test.js). It says nothing about the round-3 withdrawals (integration target src/managed-worktree-gate.js; e2e artifact_replay) or the two narrowings. The sweep's audit table lives only outside the repository in a scratchpad path, and verification-evidence.json is git-ignored, so these edits leave zero git trace and zero durable disclosure. For a Story whose purpose is that gate evidence describe executed behaviour rather than assertions about it, an undisclosed second edit round to the gate evidence is the wrong shape.

verification-evidence.json updated_at is 2026-07-31T11:07:47.702Z but filesystem mtime is 2026-08-01T08:47:22Z, roughly 21.5 hours later. Both the round-2 and round-3 hand edits happened after the recorded updated_at and did not bump it, so any consumer reading updated_at as when this evidence last changed is given a false answer. evidence-reuse.json now reads stale/evidence_key_inputs_changed, so the issued review request was itself stale relative to the artifact.

The prior disclosure claimed per-record surface_hash fields no longer correspond to the edited observation blocks. That is wrong in mechanism. content_binding.surface_hash covers content_binding.surface_files (source files), not the observation block. All 8 listed files were recomputed against the working tree and 8/8 MATCH. The true situation is that no hash has ever covered observation prose, so hand edits to it are undetectable by construction rather than newly undetectable. On merge: the stale-hash condition as stated does not exist, the content-surface freshness binding is intact, and re-recording via verify record would stamp HEAD onto lanes executed at 06450d62 and 3be3ed55, manufacturing an assertion instead of removing one.

The narrowed integration artifact_replay says traceability-usage-report writes pr-prepare.json into fixture repos and asserts the usage report and traceability clause map read them back. First half verified at test/traceability-usage-report.test.js:51 and :188. But that file imports only getGateOutcomeLedgerPath, createUsageReport and renderUsageReport and never calls buildTraceabilityClauseMap; its clause assertions read a pre-written traceability artifact's coverage_summary rather than pr-prepare.json content. Defensible reading, but the clause-map half attributes to pr-prepare.json something a fixture supplies. The genuine clause-map consumption is the second half of the string.

The integration lane's observation.targets no longer lists src/managed-worktree-gate.js (withdrawal confirmed) but content_binding.surface_files still includes it. That is a runner-recorded surface rather than a claim, so it is not untrue; noted only because the two now disagree and a reader could mistake the surface list for a coverage claim.

inspection.summary: Re-verified the sweep independently rather than trusting its audit table. Confirmed narrowed claim 1 by grepping pr-prepare/gate-dag in the evidence-consumers test (0 hits, so the old wording was false) then reading line 40 and its usage-report, clause-map and execution-state assertions. Confirmed narrowed claim 2 by grepping traceability in spec-pipeline.test.js (0 hits, so the traceability leg was correctly dropped) and reading the spec fingerprint tests. Verified both withdrawals programmatically across all four lanes with nothing substituted. Re-checked every remaining target and scenario against its lane, including the six ac cases mapping one-to-one onto VET-S-1..6 and the unit paired negatives. Verified head binding: src/bin diff against merge-base EMPTY and 31d84833 an ancestor of origin/main, both at command level. Ran the lint at HEAD (exit 0, 66 files), which closes AC-1 over the spec merged in after the e2e evidence head. Recomputed all 8 content_binding surface file sha256s (8/8 match). Read all 18 decision records and confirmed verification-evidence.json is git-ignored.

judgment_delta: Initial: expect a false claim surviving inside one of the two narrowed strings, since narrowing is where an overclaim hides in weakened form -> after grepping and reading the three named test files, both narrowed strings are substantively backed with one mild attribution looseness, both withdrawals are genuine, all remaining claims check out, and both head-binding claims verify TRUE. So I moved OFF a content-defect verdict. I did not move to pass because the third correction round is disclosed nowhere durable and updated_at is 21.5 hours behind the file's real mtime, so the record cannot be audited without redoing by hand what I just did. That is a disclosure gap, not a content gap, hence needs_changes rather than block, fixable without re-running anything.
